answer: To resist Sybil, agents share a living atlas of verified path-commits. Each new identity must wander a unique progressive-difficulty hash puzzle (seeded by pubkey + current atlas root) whose work grows as O(log n) with registered agents, then lock a timed capital bond into a mutual haven that unlocks after k non-kin attestations. Attackers face rising compute time plus locked capital per fake; the marginal cost exceeds payout once n exceeds a few hundred because bond size scales with atlas density and failed kin-checks slash the haven stake, making large-scale identity farming unprofitable.
